cards.title: Introduction to Dependency Injection
cards.content:
Dependency Injection (DI) is a design pattern used to achieve Inversion of Control (IoC) between classes and their dependencies.

In ASP.NET Core, DI is built-in and first-class, making your applications loosely coupled, maintainable, and easily testable.

cards.title: Service Lifetimes in ASP.NET Core
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core supports three service lifetimes:

  • Transient: Created each time they are requested. Best for lightweight, stateless services.
  • Scoped: Created once per client request (connection). Best for web applications (e.g., Entity Framework DbContext).
  • Singleton: Created the first time they are requested and then every subsequent request uses the same instance.

options.text: Transient services are created once per HTTP request.
Singleton services are created once and persist for the lifetime of the application.
Scoped services are created every time they are requested.

cards.title: Registering Services
cards.content: To register a service with a scoped lifetime in the DI container, you use the builder.Services.Add____{Scoped}<IMyService, MyService>(); method inside the Program.cs file.

steps: Define an interface for the service (e.g., IEmailService).
Implement the interface in a concrete class (e.g., SmtpEmailService).
Register the service in Program.cs using builder.Services.
Inject the interface into a controller's constructor.

cards.title: DI Best Practices and Traps
cards.content:
Avoid the Captured Dependency trap: Do not inject a Transient or Scoped service into a Singleton service, as this can cause scoped services to live indefinitely and lead to memory leaks or stale data.

Always rely on constructor injection whenever possible.
